newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - Nov 19.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - Nov 19.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Bangladesh press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

The ruling Awami League has reiterated its invitation to the main opposition Bangladesh Nationalist Party to sit for a dialogue for ending the impasse arising out of BNP's abstention from current session of Jatiya Sangsad (parliament).
President Shahabuddin Ahmed is likely to take an initiative to resolve the impasse arising out of ongoing dispute between the ruling Awami League and opposition BNP.
Eleven people including a police constable received bullet injuries in a gunfight between rival smugglers at a market in Amin Bazar (at Savar north of Dhaka) on Sunday.

A BNP delegation called on President Shahabuddin Ahmed at Bangabhaban Monday night and handed a memorandum alleging, among other things, that BNP members were not given sufficient time and opportunity in parliament to express their views.
Inspector General of Police M. Azizul Huq directed senior police officials on Monday to further strengthen the safety and security measures for the people.

Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina has expressed her satisfaction over the eagerness of expatriate Bangladeshis in the development efforts of their country and asked them to put their savings in investment for the country's progress.

Members of the Dhaka Stock Exchange, likely to be affected by the latest regulatory order of the Securities and Exchange Commission, are planning to contest it in court. The SEC has barred directors of listed companies from remaining or becoming members of the stock exchange.
Bangladesh has tremendous potential to explore new markets abroad, especially in European countries, through switching over to diversifying of jute products.
